appearance: This senior forest spirit appears larger and more commanding than lesser forest beings. Its tail is exceptionally full and brushlike, leaving sweeping marks in the forest duff that form patterns resembling ancient Maya glyphs when viewed from above. The coyote spirit oversees this agreement, punishing violations with crop failures and protecting compliant farmers with abundant harvests. It guards entrances to caves and cenotes serving as portals to the underworld and the realm of the rain god Chaac. People seeking to enter these sacred spaces must first encounter the coyote spirit, who assesses their intentions and grants passage or bars the way with bewildering fog.
